name: tt-vo-1
text: Two towers taller than Qutub Minar... and India's Supreme Court ordered them blown up. Noida. 28 August 2022. Gone in seconds. [short pause] But why would a court destroy towers nobody ever lived in? It starts with a garden. In 2009, the builder's revised plan put two new towers on the green space promised to residents. Then the plan grew. Twenty-four floors... became forty. Here's the problem. The towers stood just nine metres from an existing building. The rules asked for sixteen. And the residents? Nobody asked them. [short pause] So they went to court. In 2014, the High Court said... demolish. In 2021, the Supreme Court agreed, and said Noida's own planning authority had colluded. Buyers got their money back... with twelve percent interest. Then came 3,700 kilos of explosives. A ten-year fight... over in seconds. So was tearing them down the right call... or a waste?
